3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("psych", "ggplot2"))
library(psych)
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# === 01 · Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) ===
items <- c("esg1", "esg2", "esg3", "esg4", "norm1", "norm2", "norm3", "norm4", "intent1", "intent2", "intent3")
d_items <- d[, items, drop = FALSE]
n <- nrow(d_items)

# ---- EFA: suitability ----
library(psych)
R_cor <- cor(d_items)
kmo_val <- psych::KMO(R_cor)$MSA
cat("KMO:", round(kmo_val, 3), "\n")
bart_obj <- psych::cortest.bartlett(R_cor, n = n)
cat("Bartlett chisq:", round(bart_obj$chisq, 1), "df:", bart_obj$df, "p:", bart_obj$p.value, "\n")

# ---- Parallel analysis for retention ----
x <- as.matrix(d_items); nsim <- 500L; seed <- 20260619L; kind <- "fa"
set.seed(seed)
n_pa <- nrow(x); p_pa <- ncol(x)
R_pa <- cor(x); smc_v <- psych::smc(R_pa); smc_v <- pmin(pmax(smc_v, 0), 1); diag(R_pa) <- smc_v
obs_eig <- sort(eigen(R_pa, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values, decreasing = TRUE)
sim_e <- matrix(0, nsim, p_pa)
for (i in seq_len(nsim)) {
  rx <- matrix(rnorm(n_pa * p_pa), n_pa, p_pa)
  Rs <- cor(rx); sv <- psych::smc(Rs); sv <- pmin(pmax(sv, 0), 1); diag(Rs) <- sv
  sim_e[i, ] <- sort(eigen(Rs, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values, decreasing = TRUE)
}
sim_p95 <- apply(sim_e, 2, quantile, probs = 0.95)
k_retain <- 0L
for (i in seq_len(p_pa)) { if (obs_eig[i] > sim_p95[i]) k_retain <- k_retain + 1L else break }
cat("Parallel analysis retain:", k_retain, "\n")

# ---- psych::fa ----
fm_method <- "pa"
fa_obj <- psych::fa(d_items, nfactors = k_retain, fm = fm_method, rotate = "oblimin")
cat("\n--- Table 2: Variance explained ---\n")
print(round(fa_obj$Vaccounted, 3))
cat("\n--- Table 3: Rotated loadings + communalities ---\n")
load_mat <- unclass(fa_obj$loadings)
h2 <- fa_obj$communality
out_mat <- cbind(load_mat, communality = h2)
print(round(out_mat, 3))

# ---- Phi: interfactor correlations (oblique) ----
if (!is.null(fa_obj$Phi)) {
  cat("\n--- Table 4: Interfactor correlations (Phi) ---\n")
  print(round(fa_obj$Phi, 3))
}

\includegraphics{figures/01_efa/figure_scree.png}

Check KMO ($>$ .60 acceptable, $>$ .70 preferred; Kaiser \& Rice, 1974) and a significant Bartlett's test (p $<$ .001) for suitability. Parallel analysis (Horn, 1965) is the recommended retention rule - it corrects the upward bias of the Kaiser eigenvalue $>$ 1 rule (Zwick \& Velicer, 1986). Table 3 shows the rotated pattern matrix: each loading is the unique contribution of the factor to that item. Loadings |$<$ .32| (\textasciitilde{}10\% variance) are suppressed; a loading $\ge$ .32 on two or more factors flags a cross-loader (Tabachnick \& Fidell). For oblique rotation (oblimin), the Φ matrix shows interfactor correlations - if all |Φ| $<$ .32, orthogonal rotation (varimax) may be preferred. EFA is exploratory - it discovers structure; to confirm a proposed factor structure run a CFA, ideally on a separate sample (Watkins, 2018).

EFA (KMO = .83, Bartlett's $\chi$\textsuperscript{2}(55) = 2117.6, p $<$ .001) with parallel analysis retained 3 factors explaining 63.3\% of variance (oblimin rotation).

Statistical basis: KMO sampling-adequacy verbal labels ($\ge$ .60 acceptable, $\ge$ .70 preferred) (Kaiser, H. F., Rice, J. (1974). "Little Jiffy, Mark IV." Educational and Psychological Measurement, 34(1), 111-117.); Parallel analysis as the preferred factor-retention rule (Horn, J. L. (1965). "A rationale and test for the number of factors in factor analysis." Psychometrika, 30(2), 179-185.); Kaiser eigenvalue $>$ 1 rule systematically over-extracts (Zwick, W. R., Velicer, W. F. (1986). "Comparison of five rules for determining the number of components to retain." Psychological Bulletin, 99(3), 432-442.); EFA best-practice reporting standard (Watkins, M. W. (2018). "Exploratory Factor Analysis: A Guide to Best Practice." Journal of Black Psychology, 44(3), 219-246.).

Harness README
# 44 · Exploratory factor analysis (EFA)

**Question:** underlying factors behind a set of items

**Scenario:** Tourism ESG: do ESG perception, norm, and intention form three distinct factors?

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `tourism-esg.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** extraction: PAF; rotation: oblimin (explicit); retention: parallel analysis; loadings |< .32| suppressed

**Role assignments** (drag column → slot):

| Column | Role slot |
|---|---|
| `esg1` | items |
| `esg2` | items |
| `esg3` | items |

| `norm2` | items |
